state: The author of a Can application is an AI coding agent that should need very few memorized language rules. It can initially write approximate Given/When/Then source; the desired development tool responds with concrete valid Can suggestions and checks them. Existing analysis has stable codes and spans, parser recovery, and stale-edit guards but ships zero syntax repairs. Unknown constructs remain errors until valid source is chosen, particularly for roles, writes, guard/effect order and independently authored examples. Jev is a fast probabilistic evaluator of predeclared choices rather than a string/code generator. Assess an initial solution for learning speed, semantic fidelity, token economy and implementation burden.

starting_design.instructions: Which starting mechanism is most suitable for turning an agent's invalid Can attempt into a checked, reviewable correction without silently selecting business intent?

criteria.deterministic_candidates: A bounded compiler-owned candidate set from expected productions and resolved names/types is rechecked and Jev ranks its legal patches; this gives exact feedback for covered patterns but not every invented form.
criteria.layered_candidates: Compiler suggestions are supplemented by a generative patch source for unmatched forms, with deterministic checking and Jev ranking of valid results; this reaches more forms with additional model cost and moving parts.
criteria.agent_repair: The original agent receives precise errors plus minimal canonical examples and edits itself, while Jev can indicate a likely issue class; this reuses the agent but may spend more turns.
criteria.implicit_normalization: The compiler accepts a best-match rewrite as the program and displays the rewrite to the agent; it reduces friction but a best match can embed a wrong policy or effect.
